params.body:
Looking for what was worth refactoring, this is what the measurement found, and it is not "the big
files are big".

`catch (Exception $e)` in a namespaced file without `use Exception;` resolves to
`App\Http\Controllers\Settings\Exception` — a class that does not exist — so the catch never matches
and the exception walks straight past it. **Fifty-nine of them stood in this codebase**, in sixteen
files, almost all of them the settings controllers. Six other `catch (Exception)` elsewhere do have
the import and work fine.

**And repairing them would have been worse than removing them.** This is what those bodies hold:

| | |
|---|---|
| 45x | `echo 'Caught exception: ', $e->getMessage()` — the internal message in the page, and a blank one after it |
| 10x | empty |
| 2x | `return 400;` |
| 1x | `throw $e;` |
| 1x | a real answer (see below) |

Add the missing import and a dealer starts reading our exception messages on his screen. So they go:
what happens today — Laravel catches it, logs it, shows its error page — is what should happen, and
now the code says so instead of pretending otherwise. Fifty-six removed, no behaviour changed, 212
lines fewer.

**Three are left standing**, with a finding rather than a change, because they meant something and
touching them changes what the browser sees: `UserController::update` wants to answer the user modal
with JSON and a 500 (there is a dated comment above it explaining exactly why), and two AJAX
endpoints in `OwnStockController` carry `return 400` — which would not even return a 400 status,
but the string "400" with a 200. What those two should answer depends on what the JavaScript on the
other side expects, and that is a decision, not a cleanup. Until then a 500 is at least honest.

**PHPStan's baseline shrinks from 2.058 to 1.959.** Twenty-six of its entries were about exactly
this — the analyser had been pointing at it the whole time, and the first thing we did with it was
write those findings into a baseline. Nothing new went in with the regeneration; I diffed the two
baselines to be sure (26 gone, 0 added).

1.821 tests green, and `php -l` on every touched file: the removal is mechanical, so the risk was
indentation, not behaviour.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: Fifty-six catch blocks that could never catch anything
